#!/bin/bash
# Sets up the Wine prefix and installs the game's Windows prerequisites.
#
# - Creates the prefix with the Wine Mono/Gecko install prompts turned off. Under Xvfb
#   those prompts wait forever for a click, so wineboot never finishes the 32-bit
#   (syswow64) half and every 32-bit program, GlobalAgenda.exe included, fails with
#   "could not load kernel32.dll, status c0000135".
# - Rebuilds the prefix if syswow64 is missing or nearly empty.
# - Runs each installer from 17020/PreReqs once, with Steam's own switches
#   (17020/installscript.vdf). VC++ 2005 and PhysX are what the server needs. .NET 3.5
#   and the DirectX web setup don't install under Wine; they're tried once and skipped.
#
# Every Wine call is time-limited so a stuck dialog can't hang an update.
# Results go to amp-wine-setup.log next to this script.
cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1
BASE="$(pwd)"
export WINEPREFIX="$BASE/.wine" WINEDEBUG=-all
PRE="$BASE/17020/PreReqs"
LOG="$BASE/amp-wine-setup.log"
echo "== $(date -u '+%F %T') $(/usr/bin/wine --version)" >> "$LOG"

wow64_count() { ls "$WINEPREFIX/drive_c/windows/syswow64" 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }

if [ "$(wow64_count)" -lt 100 ]; then
    echo "creating Wine prefix" >> "$LOG"
    /usr/bin/wineserver -k 2>/dev/null
    rm -rf "$WINEPREFIX"
    WINEDLLOVERRIDES="mscoree,mshtml=" timeout 600 /usr/bin/xvfb-run -a \
        sh -c '/usr/bin/wineboot --init; /usr/bin/wineserver -w' >> "$LOG" 2>&1
    echo "syswow64 entries: $(wow64_count)" >> "$LOG"
fi

install() {   # install required|optional <name> <installer> <switches...>
    local kind="$1" marker="$WINEPREFIX/.ga-prereq-$2" exe="$3"; shift 3
    [ -f "$marker" ] && return 0
    if [ ! -f "$PRE/$exe" ]; then echo "skip $exe: not in PreReqs" >> "$LOG"; return 0; fi
    echo "-- $(date -u '+%T') $exe $*" >> "$LOG"
    WINEDLLOVERRIDES="mscoree=n,b;mshtml=" timeout 600 /usr/bin/xvfb-run -a \
        /usr/bin/wine "$PRE/$exe" "$@" >> "$LOG" 2>&1
    local rc=$?
    timeout 60 /usr/bin/wineserver -w
    /usr/bin/wineserver -k 2>/dev/null
    echo "exit code $rc" >> "$LOG"
    # Success is 0, or 194 (3010 = done, reboot wanted). Optional ones are only tried once.
    if [ $rc -eq 0 ] || [ $rc -eq 194 ] || [ "$kind" = optional ]; then touch "$marker"; fi
}

# The server hook is dinput8.dll (GlobalAgenda.exe imports DINPUT8 at startup; it never
# loads version.dll by itself under Wine). control-server sets WINEDLLOVERRIDES to
# version=n,b only, so prefer the game's own dinput8.dll through the prefix registry.
WINEDLLOVERRIDES="mscoree,mshtml=" timeout 120 /usr/bin/wine reg add 'HKCU\Software\Wine\DllOverrides' /v dinput8 /d native,builtin /f >> "$LOG" 2>&1
timeout 60 /usr/bin/wineserver -w

install required vcredist vcredist.exe   /Q
install required physx    physx.exe      /passive /norestart
install optional dotnet35 dotnetfx35.exe /qb
install optional directx  dxwebsetup.exe /Q

if ls "$WINEPREFIX"/drive_c/windows/syswow64/PhysXLoader.dll >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "check: PhysXLoader.dll present" >> "$LOG"
else
    echo "check: PhysXLoader.dll MISSING" >> "$LOG"
fi
exit 0

UpdateStageName: Set Up Wine Prefix and Game Prerequisites

#!/bin/bash
# Applies the "Node" settings from AMP's Configuration page to control-server.json.
# Runs as a pre-start step:
#   amp-node-config.sh <role> <node id> <node key> <master host:port> <update mode> [require]
#   role keep   -> change nothing (the default, for hand-edited configs)
#   role master -> standalone server: role "master", node block removed
#   role node   -> role "node" plus the node block, apply_content, db_path node.db, content_dir
# Everything else in control-server.json is kept. The file is only rewritten when something
# changes, and the previous version is saved as control-server.json.bak-amp.
# "require" (used by the node template): if the node settings can't be applied, the step fails,
# so AMP doesn't start the server as a standalone one by mistake.
# Results (never the key) go to amp-node-config.log.
ROLE="$1"; NODE_ID="$2"; NODE_KEY="$3"; MASTER="$4"; MODE="$5"; REQUIRE="$6"
cd "$(dirname "$0")" || { [ "$REQUIRE" = require ] && exit 1; exit 0; }
CFG="control-server.json"
LOG="amp-node-config.log"
log() { echo "$(date -u '+%F %T') $*" >> "$LOG"; }
# Couldn't apply: a log line, and in require mode a failed start.
skip() {
    log "$*"
    if [ "$REQUIRE" = require ]; then echo "amp-node-config: $*" >&2; exit 1; fi
    exit 0
}

case "$ROLE" in
    keep|"") exit 0 ;;
    master|node) ;;
    *) skip "unknown server role '$ROLE' -- control-server.json left as is" ;;
esac
if [ "$ROLE" = node ]; then
    [ -z "$MODE" ] && MODE=apply
    errors=""
    [ -z "$NODE_ID" ] && errors="$errors node ID is empty;"
    echo "$NODE_KEY" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$' || errors="$errors node key isn't 64 hex characters;"
    echo "$MASTER" | grep -Eq '^[^:[:space:]]+:[0-9]{1,5}$' || errors="$errors master address isn't host:port;"
    case "$MODE" in apply|stage|off) ;; *) errors="$errors update mode '$MODE' isn't apply, stage or off;" ;; esac
    if [ -n "$errors" ]; then
        skip "node settings not applied:$errors set them under Configuration > Global Agenda > Node. control-server.json left as is"
    fi
fi
if [ ! -f "$CFG" ]; then skip "no $CFG yet (run Update first) -- nothing to apply"; fi
if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then skip "jq is missing in this container -- control-server.json left as is"; fi
if ! jq empty "$CFG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    skip "$CFG isn't plain JSON (comments or a typo?) -- left as is; fix it or edit the role by hand"
fi

TMP="$CFG.amp-tmp"
if [ "$ROLE" = node ]; then
    jq --arg id "$NODE_ID" --arg key "$NODE_KEY" --arg master "$MASTER" --arg mode "$MODE" '
        .role = "node"
        | .node = {id: $id, key: $key, master_addr: $master, update_mode: $mode}
        | .apply_content = true
        | .db_path = "node.db"
        | .content_dir = (.content_dir // "content")
    ' "$CFG" > "$TMP"
    summary="node '$NODE_ID' -> master $MASTER, update_mode $MODE"
else
    jq '
        .role = "master"
        | del(.node, .apply_content)
        | if .db_path == "node.db" then .db_path = "server.db" else . end
    ' "$CFG" > "$TMP"
    summary="standalone server"
fi
if [ ! -s "$TMP" ] || ! jq empty "$TMP" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    rm -f "$TMP"; skip "could not build the new $CFG -- left as is"
fi
if jq -S . "$CFG" | cmp -s - <(jq -S . "$TMP"); then
    rm -f "$TMP"; exit 0   # already up to date
fi
cp -p "$CFG" "$CFG.bak-amp"
chmod 600 "$TMP" 2>/dev/null
mv "$TMP" "$CFG"
log "applied: $summary (previous file saved as $CFG.bak-amp)"
exit 0

#!/bin/bash
# Shows a node's connection to its Commonwealth master on AMP's Status page.
# AMP colours a port green while something on this machine listens on it. So while
# control-server has an open TCP connection to the master (node.master_addr in
# control-server.json), this opens a status-only listener on 127.0.0.1:<port>, and
# closes it when the connection drops; the "Master Link" port then goes red.
# Runs as a pre-start step: amp-master-link.sh [port, default 9021]. It detaches,
# so the server starts straight away, and stops when control-server stops.
# Does nothing on a standalone server. Changes go to amp-master-link.log.
cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 0
PORT="${1:-9021}"
CFG="control-server.json"
LOG="amp-master-link.log"
PIDFILE="amp-master-link.pid"
log() { echo "$(date -u '+%F %T') $*" >> "$LOG"; }
is_indicator() { tr '\0' ' ' < "/proc/$1/cmdline" 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'amp-master-link\.sh'; }

# Read role and master_addr without jq, skipping // comment lines.
cfg_value() {
    sed 's#^[[:space:]]*//.*##' "$CFG" 2>/dev/null \
        | grep -o "\"$1\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"[^\"]*\"" | head -n 1 | sed 's/.*"\([^"]*\)"$/\1/'
}

if [ "$2" != "--run" ]; then
    # Stop the indicator left from the previous start (only if that PID really is one).
    OLD="$(cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null)"
    if [ -n "$OLD" ] && is_indicator "$OLD"; then
        kill "$OLD" 2>/dev/null
        for ((i = 0; i < 20; i++)); do is_indicator "$OLD" || break; sleep 0.5; done
    fi
    rm -f "$PIDFILE"
    [ "$(cfg_value role)" = node ] || exit 0
    [ -n "$(cfg_value master_addr)" ] || { log "role is node but there's no master_addr in $CFG; indicator off"; exit 0; }
    if [ -f "$LOG" ] && [ "$(wc -l < "$LOG")" -gt 2000 ]; then
        tail -n 1000 "$LOG" > "$LOG.tmp" && mv "$LOG.tmp" "$LOG"
    fi
    # Detach with no handles on AMP's output pipes, so this step returns at once.
    if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        setsid bash "$0" "$PORT" --run </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 3>&- 4>&- 5>&- 6>&- 7>&- 8>&- 9>&- &
    else
        nohup bash "$0" "$PORT" --run </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 3>&- 4>&- 5>&- 6>&- 7>&- 8>&- 9>&- &
    fi
    exit 0
fi

MASTER="$(cfg_value master_addr)"
HOST="${MASTER%:*}"
MPORT="${MASTER##*:}"
case "$MPORT" in ''|*[!0-9]*) log "can't read a port from master_addr '$MASTER'; indicator off"; exit 0 ;; esac

# /proc/net/tcp shows IPv4 addresses as little-endian hex and ports as big-endian hex.
hexip() { local IFS=.; set -- $1; printf '%02X%02X%02X%02X' "$4" "$3" "$2" "$1"; }
TARGETS=""
resolve() {
    local ips ip t=""
    if [[ "$HOST" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        ips="$HOST"
    else
        ips="$(getent ahostsv4 "$HOST" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}' | sort -u)"
    fi
    [ -z "$ips" ] && return   # DNS failed: keep the addresses from last time
    for ip in $ips; do t="$t $(hexip "$ip"):$(printf '%04X' "$MPORT")"; done
    TARGETS="$t"
}
# An ESTABLISHED (01) TCP connection to the master, IPv4 or IPv4-mapped IPv6.
connected() {
    local t
    for t in $TARGETS; do
        grep -qE "^ *[0-9]+: [0-9A-F]+:[0-9A-F]{4} (0000000000000000FFFF0000)?$t 01 " \
            /proc/net/tcp /proc/net/tcp6 2>/dev/null && return 0
    done
    return 1
}
cs_running() {
    local c n
    for c in /proc/[0-9]*/comm; do
        read -r n 2>/dev/null < "$c" && [ "$n" = control-server ] && return 0
    done
    return 1
}

# The listener accepts and drops connections, and quits if this script goes away,
# so a killed indicator can't leave the port stuck green.
LPID=""
open_port() {
    if command -v perl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        perl -MSocket -e '
            my $parent = getppid();
            socket(S, PF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0) or die "socket: $!\n";
            setsockopt(S, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, pack("l", 1));
            bind(S, pack_sockaddr_in($ARGV[0], inet_aton("127.0.0.1"))) or die "bind 127.0.0.1:$ARGV[0]: $!\n";
            listen(S, 5) or die "listen: $!\n";
            while (getppid() == $parent) {
                my $rin = ""; vec($rin, fileno(S), 1) = 1;
                if (select(my $rout = $rin, undef, undef, 5) > 0) { close(C) if accept(C, S); }
            }' "$PORT" 2> amp-master-link.err &
    elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        python3 -c '
import os, socket, sys
parent = os.getppid()
s = socket.socket()
s.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
s.bind(("127.0.0.1", int(sys.argv[1])))
s.listen(5)
s.settimeout(5)
while os.getppid() == parent:
    try:
        s.accept()[0].close()
    except socket.timeout:
        pass' "$PORT" 2> amp-master-link.err &
    elif command -v socat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        socat "TCP-LISTEN:$PORT,bind=127.0.0.1,reuseaddr,fork" /dev/null 2> amp-master-link.err &
    else
        return 2
    fi
    LPID=$!
}
port_open() { [ -n "$LPID" ] && kill -0 "$LPID" 2>/dev/null; }
close_port() {
    if [ -n "$LPID" ]; then kill "$LPID" 2>/dev/null; wait "$LPID" 2>/dev/null; fi
    LPID=""
}

trap 'close_port; [ "$(cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null)" = "$$" ] && rm -f "$PIDFILE"' EXIT
trap 'exit 0' TERM INT HUP
echo $$ > "$PIDFILE"
nap() { sleep "$1" & wait $!; }   # lets TERM through straight away

# This step runs just before control-server starts, so give it a moment.
for ((i = 0; i < 60; i++)); do cs_running && break; nap 2; done
cs_running || { log "control-server didn't start; indicator off"; exit 0; }

STATE=""
N=0
while cs_running; do
    (( N++ % 60 == 0 )) && resolve   # every 5 minutes, in case the master's DNS changes
    if connected; then
        if ! port_open; then
            open_port
            if [ $? -eq 2 ]; then log "no perl, python3 or socat in this container; can't open the status port"; exit 0; fi
            nap 1
            if ! port_open; then
                [ "$STATE" != failed ] && log "couldn't open status port $PORT: $(head -c 300 amp-master-link.err 2>/dev/null)"
                STATE=failed
                nap 25
                continue
            fi
        fi
        NEW=up
    else
        close_port
        NEW=down
    fi
    if [ "$NEW" != "$STATE" ]; then
        if [ "$NEW" = up ]; then
            log "connected to master $MASTER; status port $PORT open"
        else
            log "not connected to master $MASTER; status port $PORT closed"
        fi
        STATE="$NEW"
    fi
    nap 5
done
log "control-server stopped; status port $PORT closed"

#!/bin/bash
# Writes a starter control-server.json on first install only.
# Updates never overwrite an existing control-server.json, so edit it freely.
cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1
mkdir -p logs crashes
[ -f control-server.json ] && exit 0
BASE="$(pwd)"
tok() { head -c 32 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n'; }
cat > control-server.json <<EOF
{
    "wine_binary": "/usr/bin/wine",
    "wine_prefix": "${BASE}/.wine",
    "xvfb_run_path": "/usr/bin/xvfb-run",
    "game_binary": "${BASE}/17020/Binaries/GlobalAgenda.exe",
    "host": "127.0.0.1",
    "nat_networks": "",
    "nat_ip": "",
    "home_map_name": "Dome3_VR_Arena_P",
    "home_map_game_mode": "TgGame.TgGame_Mission",
    "tcp_port": 9000,
    "chat_port": 9001,
    "ipc_port": 9010,
    "udp_port_range": { "lo": 9002, "hi": 9020 },
    "admin_token": "$(tok)",
    "overlay_http_port": 0,
    "overlay_token": "$(tok)",
    "startup_timeout_seconds": 300,
    "db_path": "${BASE}/server.db",
    "crash_dir": "Z:${BASE}/crashes",
    "log_dir": "Z:${BASE}/logs",
    "fix_package_guids": false,
    "clear_logs": true,
    "use_docker": false,
    "per_slot_prefix": false,
    "enabled_channels": [],
    "enabled_crash_channels": [],
    "announcers": []
}
EOF
chmod 600 control-server.json
